articles.name: Why are my sent emails getting marked as spam?
articles.title: Why are my sent emails getting marked as spam?
articles.body:
Let's say you send an email, only to have the recipient discover it hours later in their Spam folder.

Spam filtering is performed by email providers to protect their recipients from unsolicited or malicious emails. No spam filters are perfect, and they may cause your legitimate email to be marked as spam.

It's often difficult to know why a message was filtered as spam. In this help page, we'll cover the most common scenarios that might cause an email to be marked as spam on the recipient's side.

  • The email is considered bulk sending
  • Something in the email's content is considered suspicious
  • The email is not properly authenticated
  • The email address has poor domain reputation
    • Domain reputation specific to an email provider
    • Domain reputation specific to a single recipient
  • Contact support

The email is considered bulk sending

Sending bulk mail can increase the chances of your messages being marked as spam. Email providers sometimes apply stricter requirements for bulk senders, so it is generally better to use a dedicated bulk mailing service.

If your workflow involves sending marketing, newsletter, transactional, or notification emails, we ask that you please use a service dedicated to bulk mailing. Sending bulk emails is not permitted under our Terms of Service.

Something in the email's content is considered suspicious

One of the factors an email provider considers while deciding whether an email is spam is its content. Excessive use of words seen in promotional emails, links to websites or domains with a poor reputation, and signatures containing multiple links are some of the common reasons why an email may be marked as spam.

If you suspect that your email's content may be considered suspicious, you can test this by sending a plain-text email with a short sentence. If the email doesn’t go to the recipient's spam folder, the problem is almost certainly the content of the email you sent earlier.

The email is not properly authenticated

Email authentication is a set of protocols that verifies the legitimacy of the email sender, helping to control and recognize email spoofing. It uses existing standards like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to confirm that an email is genuinely from a sender authorized to use the domain it claims to be from. If the domain has not been properly set up, mail providers may mark your email as spam.

If you're using a Fastmail domain, we will take care of the necessary DNS records to have the email sent out with proper authentication.

If you're sending emails from a custom domain, make sure that your domain's DNS records are configured correctly to send emails. You can check if the SPF and DKIM configurations are correct by opening your domain from the Settings → Domains screen.

The email address has poor domain reputation

The recipient’s email provider may mark an email as spam if it is coming from a domain with a low reputation. If your domain is newly registered, this can cause it to be considered low reputation. Your domain could also have a low reputation if it has been reported for spam too many times, or if it is on a blacklist.

If you suspect that your domain’s reputation is causing the issue, you can test this by sending the same email again, but this time from an alias at a Fastmail domain instead of your custom domain. If the email doesn't go to the recipient's spam folder, the problem is likely the domain's reputation.

Domain reputation specific to an email provider

If you notice that emails addressed to only a particular email provider are being marked as spam (e.g. every message you send to someone using Outlook goes to their spam folder), it usually indicates that the domain has been blacklisted by that email provider. 

It may be helpful to ask your contacts who use the same email provider to mark your emails as "not spam," which could help increase the reputation of your domain at that provider.

Domain reputation specific to a single recipient

If your emails are only being filtered as spam when sent to a specific person, it could be caused by a specific rule, setting, or filter on that recipient's account. You can ask the recipient to:

  • Review their mailbox rules or filters to see if emails from your address or domain are being asked to be marked as spam.
  • Add your email address or domain to their Safe Senders/Allowed Senders list.
  • Contact their email administrator if they are a part of an organization to verify that they aren’t filtering the your address or domain.

Contact support

If you’re unable to narrow down the issue, ask the recipient for the full headers of the email that was marked as spam. These headers may contain information about why an email was marked as spam.

Contact our support team with these headers and the details of the troubleshooting steps you’ve already performed, and we can look into this further.

articles.name: VIP contacts
articles.title: VIP contacts
articles.body:
You can mark certain contacts in your address book as VIP contacts. You can choose special settings for your VIP contact group, including receiving notifications for messages from these contacts only.

VIP contacts will be displayed with a star icon next to their name, and messages from these contacts will appear with a star icon in your mailbox.

To mark a contact as a VIP, open the contact in your Contacts screen and click the star icon in the upper right corner. You can also right-click the contact and select Add to VIPs. 

If you need to remove a contact from your VIP contacts, you can do so by clicking the star again or right-clicking the contact and selecting Remove from VIPs.

You can view all of your VIP contacts by clicking on the VIPs group under All contacts.

You can search for all messages from your VIP contacts by entering fromin:vips in your mailbox's Search Mail bar.

Notifications can be enabled for VIP contacts only. For more information, please see our Getting desktop notifications help page.

articles.name: Setting up Squarespace with Fastmail
articles.title: Setting up Squarespace with Fastmail
articles.body:
If you have a domain that is managed by Squarespace, it can be set up with Fastmail for email hosting. The DNS records for the domain will need to be updated in order to properly configure it.

Squarespace has an automatic setup option and a manual setup option for adding the DNS records.

  • Automatic setup
  • Manual setup

Automatic setup

Squarespace offers a third-party email preset for Fastmail that allows you to easily set up your Squarespace domain with Fastmail.

To add the preset, follow these steps:

  1. Open your Squarespace domains dashboard.
  2. Click the domain you're setting up.
  3. In the side panel, click DNS.
  4. Click Add preset in the top-right corner, then select Fastmail from the dropdown menu.
  5. Enter your password, or if you have two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled, you'll need to reauthenticate your account with your 2FA method. Click Continue.
  6. Click Add to add the preset.

If you need any help setting up the preset, Squarespace support should be able to provide assistance.

Manual setup

If preferred, you can manually set up DNS records for your domain.

  1. Open your Squarespace domains dashboard.
  2. Click the domain you're setting up.
  3. In the side panel, click DNS, then click DNS Settings.
  4. Scroll down to Custom Records.
  5. Click Add record and enter in the information for the record.
    • Please refer to the Setting up your domain: MX only page for the required DNS records. You'll need to add records for MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
  6. Click Save to add the record.
  7. Repeat this for each record that needs to be added.

If further assistance is needed, you can reach out to our support team.

articles.name: Choosing your data residency
articles.title: Choosing your data residency
articles.body:
Effective August 2026, Fastmail customers can opt to have their data stored in the European Union, encrypted at rest on Fastmail-owned secure servers in Amsterdam.

At launch, existing customers with a billing address in Europe (including EU-neighboring countries such as the UK, Switzerland, Norway) were automatically set to use EU servers, and all other customers continue to use US servers. New customers are prompted to choose a region at signup.

All customers, including trial users, have the option to choose EU or US servers, regardless of where you are located.

  • What each region means for your data
  • How to switch regions
    • Do I need to update my mail clients?
    • Do I need to update my custom domains?
  • Data transparency

What each region means for your data

EU servers

If you choose the EU option for your data residency, the primary copy of your data will be stored on our Amsterdam servers. A resilient replica of your data will be stored on our US servers.

If you are using an email address at a custom domain with Fastmail’s nameservers, or one of Fastmail’s EU region domains, incoming mail will arrive through EU servers. 

The web interface, desktop app, and mobile app will connect to EU servers. 

If our EU servers ever become unavailable, connections will fall back to one of our US locations so you can still have access to your data.

Backups, logs, and debug systems are all based in the US.

US servers

If you choose the US option for your data residency, the primary copy of your data will be stored on our US servers. A resilient replica of your data will be stored on US servers at a geographically separate secondary site.

If you are using an email address at a custom domain with Fastmail’s nameservers, or one of Fastmail’s US region domains, incoming mail will arrive through US servers.

The web interface, desktop app, and mobile app will connect to US servers. 

If a US server location ever becomes unavailable, connections fall back to our other US location so you can still have access to your data.

How to switch regions

You can change the primary data storage location by following these steps:

  1. Go to Settings → Users & Sharing → Team settings.
  2. In the Data residency section, select Change data residency.
  3. Choose US or EU, then select Save.

For multi-user accounts, this setting affects all users, and only an admin can make this change.

Once you have selected a new location for your data, your account will be added to the queue for migration to the other servers. During the migration, your Fastmail account may become temporarily unavailable, and the Fastmail web interface will show a loading screen. This will likely last a few minutes, depending on the size of the account.

Do I need to update my mail clients?

You will not need to make any updates to mail clients or other third-party apps. Your mail clients/apps should continue working without any changes.

If you prefer to use regional servers for your mail client, you are welcome to do so. 

Our EU regional servers are:

  • eu-smtp.fastmail.com
  • eu-imap.fastmail.com
  • eu-pop.fastmail.com
  • eu-caldav.fastmail.com
  • eu-carddav.fastmail.com
  • eu-myfiles.fastmail.com

Our US regional servers are: 

  • us-smtp.fastmail.com
  • us-imap.fastmail.com
  • us-pop.fastmail.com
  • us-caldav.fastmail.com
  • us-carddav.fastmail.com
  • us-myfiles.fastmail.com

If the servers you're looking for are not listed above, or if you experience any issues while trying to update your mail client's servers, please contact our support team for assistance.

Do I need to update my custom domains?

You will not need to make any updates to your custom domains. Your domains should continue working without any changes.

If you have a custom domain where the nameservers are hosted with Fastmail, the domain's MX records will be automatically updated to point to the US or EU MX servers, based on the region set for your account.

If you have a custom domain where the nameservers are hosted elsewhere, the domain's MX records will not be automatically updated. You are not required to make any changes, and your mail will work reliably regardless of the region where your data is stored. If you prefer to use our regional MX servers for your domain, you are welcome to do so.

Our EU MX servers are:

  • eu1-smtp.messagingengine.com (first, priority = 10)
  • eu2-smtp.messagingengine.com (second, priority = 20)

Our US MX servers are:

  • us1-smtp.messagingengine.com (first, priority = 10)
  • us2-smtp.messagingengine.com (second, priority = 20)

If you choose to update your MX records, please make sure that these are the only two MX records set for the domain, as having extra MX records can lead to conflicts that prevent mail from getting routed correctly.

If you experience any issues after updating your domain's DNS, please contact our support team for assistance.

Data transparency

Fastmail is an Australian company, subject to Australian law. Whether your data is stored in the US or EU, we will respond the same way to lawful requests from relevant authorities. For more information on how Fastmail responds to law enforcement, please see the "Law enforcement" section of our Fastmail privacy help page, or you can read our Data Transparency Report here.

We prioritize keeping your data safe and available to you. Please note that if you choose the EU region for your data residency, a live copy of your data is still replicated to the US. If your home location is down, you will temporarily connect to one of our other server locations so you can continue to access your data. Backups, logs, and debug systems are located in the US.

articles.name: AI Instant Answers on the support form
articles.title: AI Instant Answers on the support form
articles.body:
When you submit a support question, you have the option to get an instant answer from an AI assistant. This page explains how AI Instant Answers works, what it can and can't do, and what happens to what you enter.

  • How it works
  • What the AI can and can't help with
  • Your query and your privacy
  • Prefer to speak with a person?
  • Why did I receive a misleading response?

How it works

When you click Try AI Instant Answer, the information you have entered in the support form is sent to an AI assistant powered by Anthropic's Claude to generate a response.

The AI is trained on Fastmail's public help documentation — the same articles available in the Fastmail Help Center. It cannot access your email, your contacts, or your calendar.

What the AI can and can't help with

The AI tool works well for general questions, like how features work or how to set something up.

This tool cannot access your account, so it won't be able to do anything specific to your situation, like looking up a specific billing detail, or reviewing our internal logs to explain a mail delivery issue. If your question is about these specific details, or anything else the AI tool isn't equipped to answer, we'll display a message on the screen suggesting that you submit your query as a support ticket, which you can do on the same page: just complete the CAPTCHA if it appears, then select Create ticket.

The tool cannot process any files attached to the ticket. 

AI can make mistakes. Answers may occasionally be inaccurate, incomplete, or not reflect recent changes to Fastmail's features. You can review the Fastmail Help Center to validate information that the AI provides.

If something doesn't seem right, please click Create ticket on the same screen so a member of the Fastmail team can have a look.

Your query and your privacy

The options you select and text you type in the form are sent to Anthropic's Claude to generate a response. For more on how Fastmail handles data in connection with third-party AI services, see our privacy policy.

Since AI Instant Answer doesn't have access to your account, it doesn't need any personal details to answer your questions. Please also avoid including sensitive information like passwords or credit card numbers in your question, just as you would when sending your message to our support team.

Your interaction with AI Instant Answer is available to Fastmail staff to ensure the quality of the information we provide.

Prefer to speak with a person?

The option to create a ticket is always available. We don't require that you to interact with an AI or create barriers to getting in touch with the Fastmail team. Your support tickets always go straight to a human, and you don't have to try the AI first.

If you did try the AI and the answer didn't resolve your question, you can still send a ticket at any time — we're always happy to hear from our customers!.

I received a misleading response

The responses provided by AI Instant Answers are powered by Claude using Generative AI, which can occasionally produce responses that are incorrect or misleading. This is known as "hallucinating" information, and is a result of the limitations of Generative AI models. AI Instant Answers should not be relied upon as a source of truth. 

Please use our "Was this helpful?" prompt to indicate you're received information that was not accurate. We will use this information to improve the AI Instant Answers tool.

articles.name: Customize your mailbox
articles.title: Customize your mailbox
articles.body:
There are various ways you can customize your mailbox to fit your needs. These customization options can be found in the Settings → Display options and Settings → Mail preferences screens.

  • Display options
    • Region
    • Theme
    • Navigation
    • Accessibility
  • Mail preferences
    • Mailbox display
    • Mail organization
    • Compose and reading options

Display options

On the Settings → Display options screen, you can control your language and time settings, themes and colors, and preferred accessibility settings.

Region

The Region section includes options related to language and time preferences.

  • Language: Select your preferred language for the Fastmail interface.
  • Start week on: Choose what day your week starts on.
  • Time format: Choose what between a 12-hour clock or 24-hour clock.

Theme

In the Theme section, you can customize the appearance of your Fastmail interface. This includes choosing preferred colors, and also switching between light mode and dark mode.

Please see the Themes help page for more details.

Navigation

The navigation bar on the left-hand side of your mailbox can be customized. Enabling each option will include an icon in the navigation bar, which allows you to click and directly go to that specific screen. Disabling an option will remove the corresponding icon from the navigation bar. If all options are disabled, the navigation bar will be hidden completely.

Accessibility

The accessibility options allow you to change the Fastmail interface to fit your needs.

  • Text size: Increase or decrease text size.
  • UI Font: Change the font used in the interface. Our default font is Proxima Nova. If you prefer, you can change this to match your system font.
  • Use a monospaced font for plain text: When enabled, the font used for displaying plain text will be a monospace font.
  • Show a dividing line between rows: When enabled, there will be dividing lines displayed between rows.
  • Enable keyboard shortcuts: When enabled, keyboard shortcuts can be used. When disabled, keyboard shortcuts will not work. See the Keyboard shortcuts help page for what keyboard shortcuts are available.
  • Drag/hold activation delay: There can be a delay added for when you are performing dragging/holding actions in the interface. When the Off option is selected, dragging/holding will be immediate with no delay.

Please see the General accessibility help page for an overview of Fastmail's accessibility.

Mail preferences

On the Settings → Mail preferences screen, you can customize the look of your mailbox, how your mail is organized, and also your mail composing and reading options.

Mailbox display

  • Reading pane: Change the location of the reading pane, or disable it completely.
  • Message previews: Enable or disable message previews.
  • Hover actions: Show or hide hover actions on messages.
  • Show avatars: Show or hide avatars.

Mail organization

You can choose to organize mail using folders mode or labels mode. Switching between the two is easy, and can be done by choosing either Folders or Labels in the Organize messages with section. Please see the Setting up and using folders or Setting up and using labels help pages for more details.

Customization settings for conversations and other mail actions can be found in this section as well. Please see the Conversations help page for more details.

Compose and reading options

There are also customization settings for when you're composing, replying to, and forwarding messages. Please refer to the Compose settings section in the Composing a message help page for more details.

Reading

Remote images: Choose how you want remote images to be displayed.

View messages in: Choose to view messages in rich text or plain text.

Always show message headers: Enabling this option will automatically display the headers of a message when viewing it.

Display the following extra headers when reading messages: You can add headers that you would like to be displayed in messages. These extra headers will be displayed along with the default headers.

articles.name: Why did I get an email from myself?
articles.title: Why did I get an email from myself?
articles.body:
If you've received an email that appears to be from your own email address, but you didn’t send it, it can be alarming, especially if the message claims the sender has access to your account. The good news is that, in many cases, your account hasn’t been compromised and the email is spoofed.

This help page explains what email spoofing is, how to tell if it happened, and what you can do about it.

What is email spoofing?

Email spoofing is when someone sends an email that is made to appear as though it came from a different address or sender than it actually did, often a trusted sender, organization, or even your own email address. Attackers use spoofing to trick recipients into trusting a message or to bypass spam filters.

Spoofing is possible because the addresses you see in the To and From fields are simply part of the message content, they do not determine delivery. For example, forwarded emails maintain the original To and From while the sender (the person who forwarded the email to you) and recipient (you) are different. Behind the scenes, email is routed using separate “envelope” addresses.

Since the email system was originally designed for communication between trusted devices, To and From fields can be forged or spoofed. The Email addressing help page has more detailed information about this process.

Modern sender authentication tools can help in identifying when an email has been spoofed.

What is sender authentication?

We use Sender authentication standards like SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC to help verify that an email really came from who it claims to. SPF checks whether the sending server is allowed to send for that domain, DKIM uses cryptographic signatures so receivers can tell if the message was tampered with. DMARC builds on these by checking against the domain in the header “From” (the part that is most commonly spoofed), and by letting domain owners specify how SPF and DKIM failures should be handled.

Fastmail treats authentication results as a signal and not a cause to block emails because sender authentication can fail for legitimate reasons such as email forwarding. Not all authentication failures indicate a spoofed or malicious message. When an email fails authentication, spam scores are adjusted to reflect this. However, authentication is only one of many factors used to determine whether a message is delivered to the Inbox or Spam.

How to detect if an email was sent from your Fastmail account?

You can view the headers of an email by clicking the Actions menu at the top right of the message, then clicking Show raw message.

If the header X-ME-Sender is present and contains xms information, the email was sent from Fastmail servers which means the email was not spoofed. If you see this header on an email with your address in the “From” header and you did not send this email, please reach out to our support team for assistance.

How can I prevent spoofing?

If you receive a spoofed message, you can report it as spam by selecting the message, clicking the More button, and clicking Report spam.

If you are using a custom domain and you’re seeing frequent spoofing attempts, we recommend setting up a DMARC policy. This tells receiving mail servers how to handle unauthenticated emails sent from your domain.

articles.name: Connecting AI tools via Fastmail's MCP server
articles.title: Connecting AI tools via Fastmail's MCP server
articles.body:
MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is an open standard for how AI models interact with data sources and tools. An MCP server allows different services to connect with AI applications.

Fastmail has an MCP server that you can use to connect an AI tool to your Fastmail account, such as Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, or Perplexity. At this time, Fastmail does not offer direct integrations with any AI tools.

Use of an MCP server is optional, and is intended for customers who are expressly interested in using AI tools with their Fastmail account. For more information on our approach regarding MCP, please see our blog post.

  • What can I do with Fastmail's MCP server?
  • How do I use Fastmail's MCP server?
  • Reviewing and removing AI client access
  • Privacy and data handling

What can I do with Fastmail's MCP server?

You can use Fastmail's MCP server to connect your Fastmail account to any AI client that supports MCP and allows you to use an external server. 

Depending on how you'd like to use the AI client with your Fastmail account, you can choose some or all of the following levels of access:

  • Read-only access: The AI client can search and read your mail, contacts, and calendars.
  • Write access: The AI client can draft replies, move, delete, and organize your mail, and update your contacts and calendars.
  • Send access: The AI client can send emails on your behalf.

Examples

Below are some examples of ways you could prompt an AI client to interact with your Fastmail account.

If you grant read-only access:

  • "What's on my calendar for tomorrow?"
  • "Summarize this email for me."
  • "Create a to-do list based on emails I received in the last three days."
  • "Find Hannah's address in my contacts"

If you grant write access:

  • "Draft a reply to this email."
  • "Update the phone number for this contact."
  • "Move all messages from this company into a new folder."

If you grant send access:

  • "Send an email to Hannah informing her that I will not be at today's meeting."

How do I use Fastmail's MCP server?

Generally speaking, setup will look something like this:

  1. Add the URL for Fastmail's MCP server to your AI client's list of MCP servers. The URL is: https://api.fastmail.com/mcp
  2. Follow the steps onscreen to authenticate the connection via OAuth 2.0. (Your normal Fastmail password should be used here, so you do not need to set up an app password.) If you would prefer to use an API token instead of connecting via OAuth, you can create one.
  3. Select which levels of access you would like the AI client to have (you can choose more than one):
    • The AI client can search and read your mail, contacts, and calendars.
    • The AI client can draft replies, move, delete, and organize your mail, and update your contacts and calendars.
    • The AI client can send emails on your behalf.

The exact steps for setup will differ depending on the AI client you're using. If you need assistance finding the documentation for your AI client, please feel free to reach out to our support team, and we can guide you in the right direction.

Reviewing and removing AI client access

Once an AI client has been successfully connected to your Fastmail account, the AI client will be listed as an app under Settings → Privacy & Security → Connected apps.

You can review the AI client's access details at any time, which include the following:

  • The name of the AI client
  • What the AI client has access to
  • The date and time access was first given
  • The date, time, and IP/location of most recent access

To review an AI client's access details:

  1. Log in to the Fastmail web interface and go to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen.
  2. Find the Connected apps & API tokens section. Click Manage app passwords and access.
  3. Find the AI client and click on it. 

You can remove the AI client's access at any time. To remove it:

  1. Log in to the Fastmail web interface and go to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen.
  2. Find the Connected apps & API tokens section. Click Manage app passwords and access.
  3. Find the AI client and click on it. 
  4. Click Remove access.
  5. Click OK if you are sure you want to continue, as this action cannot be undone.
    • A Verify it's you box may appear. Enter your password and click Continue. (For more information, see our Password-protected actions help page.)
  6. You will return to the Connected apps screen, where you can confirm that the AI client has been removed.

Privacy and data handling

When you connect an AI client to your Fastmail account, any data that the AI client accesses (such as emails, calendar events, or contacts) is subject to that provider's own privacy policy and data handling practices. 

Fastmail has no control over how connected AI clients store, process, or use your data. Before connecting an AI client, we recommend reviewing its privacy policy.

Depending on your profession or location, connecting your email to a third-party AI client may have legal or compliance implications. 

If your email contains sensitive, confidential, or regulated information — such as health records, legal communications, or personal data belonging to others — you should seek appropriate advice before connecting an AI client to your account.

articles.name: Open messages in a new window
articles.title: Open messages in a new window
articles.body:
If you need to reference other emails in your mailbox, or if you just love to multi-task, you can open conversation threads or messages in new windows.

You can have multiple pop-out windows open at a time. If you adjust the size or position of a pop-out window, this will be remembered the next time you open one.

Viewing messages in a new window

You can open messages in a new window by clicking the pop-out arrow icon in the upper-right hand corner at the top of the conversation thread, next to the Print icon.

You can also open a conversation in a new window by double-clicking the conversation in your message list, or holding down the Shift key and single-clicking the conversation in your message list.

Composing, replying, or forwarding messages in a new window

You can compose messages or replies in a new window by clicking the pop-out arrow icon in the upper-right hand corner of the composer:

You can also open the composer in a new window by holding the Shift key and clicking Compose or Reply. If you prefer keyboard shortcuts, you can use Shift+R to reply in a new window, or Shift+A to reply all. 

If you open the pop-out composer while replying to a conversation or editing a draft, you will see a banner that says You are editing this draft in another window at the bottom of the conversation thread in the main window. This is to prevent accidental multiple drafts.

When you click Send or Discard, the pop-out composer will automatically close. If you have the Undo send feature enabled, the undo option will be shown in the main window.

For general information on composing messages or replies, please see our Composing a message help page.

articles.name: Setting up iOS devices: iOS 26
articles.title: Setting up iOS devices: iOS 26
articles.body:
If you have an iPhone or iPad, you can use this guide to set up your Fastmail account in your Mail app.

It's recommended to make Safari your default browser for this installation. You can change the default browser to another one of your choice afterwards. 

Did you know? Fastmail has an excellent iOS app which many of our users prefer to other mail apps. See our mobile app help for more details.

Third-party apps need their own app password to access your information. If you use your normal password or your Fastmail two step verification password on an external account, syncing to an external service won't work and you will see a password error.

  • Automatic setup tools
    • Setting up via QR code
    • Setting up via mobile web browser
  • Adding additional accounts
  • Setting up notes
  • Updating your password
  • Manual setup
  • Removing a Fastmail profile

Automatic setup tool

You can easily set up your device and avoid a lot of manual typing using our setup tools: either scan a QR code that sets everything up, or set up via a mobile web browser.

Note: Selecting contacts/CardDAV will sync all CardDAV accounts by default (both personal and shared). If you want to sync them separately, manually create individual CardDAV accounts.

As a general note, if you want to send from addresses other than your Fastmail username, you will need to set up your Fastmail account on iOS manually instead of using our automatic setup tools. However, if your Fastmail account uses a different alias as its default address, the configuration profile will use this when composing emails instead of your username.

Setting up via QR code

If you have another device nearby, you can use your camera to scan a QR code and automatically set up your Fastmail account. (Please note that the QR code will not appear if you have multiple addresses.)

  1. Log in to the Fastmail web interface on your device and go to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen.
  2. Find the Connected apps & API tokens section. Click Manage app passwords and access.
  3. Click New app password. 
    • A Verify it's you box may appear. Enter your password and click Continue. (For more information, see our Password-protected actions help page.) 
  4. Give your app password a name to indicate which device and app this password is for.
  5. For the QR code setup, you will need to choose either the Mail, Contacts & Calendars access or the Mail (IMAP/POP/SMTP) access.
  6. Click Generate password.

The screen will show a QR code.

  1. Point the Camera app on your iPhone or iPad at the QR code on the screen.
  2. Tap on the yellow link that appears. 

  3. Tap Allow to download the configuration file.

  4. You'll then see a confirmation that the profile is downloaded.

  5. Install the configuration profile: Tap Settings, then Profile Downloaded, then Install. Note: For iPad devices, after Settings, you may need to tap More for Your iPad before you get to Profile Downloaded.

     

  6. Enter your device's passcode and tap Install again.
  7. Tap Done to finish the process. This will automatically set up your mail, calendar, and contact settings on your device, according to the access types you requested for this app password.

Setting up via mobile web browser

You can use the mobile browser on your device to perform a one time automatic setup.

  1. Log in to the Fastmail web interface on your iOS device and and go to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen.
  2. Find the Connected apps & API tokens section. Click Manage app passwords and access.
  3. Click New app password. 
    • A Verify it's you box may appear. Enter your password and click Continue. (For more information, see our Password-protected actions help page.) 
  4. Give your app password a name to indicate which device and app this password is for.
  5. Choose what sort of access this password requires.
  6. Click Generate password.

The screen will show a link to a configuration file to install a new profile. Click Open this configuration file.

  1. Allow the browser to open Settings to show a configuration profile.

  2. Install the configuration profile. This will automatically set up your mail, calendar and contact settings on your device, according to the access types you requested for this app password.

Adding additional accounts

Adding other accounts to send with on iOS.

Set up notes

  1. Open the Settings app in your device. 
  2. Scroll down and tap Apps.
  3. Scroll down to the "M" section and tap Mail.
  4. Tap Mail Accounts. Select your Fastmail email account from the list.

  5. Enable the Notes option.

You can now verify it's working in the Notes application.

  1. Open the Notes app.

  2. You will now see a list of places where your notes are stored, and you can select which set of notes you want to view.

If you'd like to use Fastmail storage as the default location for new notes to ensure they are backed up and always available:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Scroll down and tap Apps.
  3. Scroll down to the "N" section and tap Notes.
  4. Select Default Account.

  5. Choose your Fastmail username as your default account.

If your notes do not display, check the advanced server settings.

Updating your password

If you change an iPhone app password after adding your Fastmail account to your iOS device, you will need to update the settings on your device. The easiest way is to delete the old profile off your device and use the automatic setup tool to generate a new password and store it on your phone.

Manual setup

To set up the app passwords for email, calendar, contacts and notes manually, we have detailed instructions. This is not the preferred way, as it is more prone to human error.

Remove a Fastmail Profile

To delete Fastmail from your iOS device, you need to remove the profile.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Scroll down and tap VPN and Device Management.
  4. Select the Fastmail profile and tap Remove Profile.

This will remove Fastmail from the list of internet accounts on that device.

It is possible to individually disable each mail, contact or calendar account in the iOS settings, but to delete them, you have to remove the profile.

articles.name: Composing a message
articles.title: Composing a message
articles.body:
When composing a message, there are various customization options available. You can edit these customization options to fit your sending preferences.

  • The composer
    • Compose in a new window
    • Sending replies
    • Adding recipients
    • Composer toolbar actions
      • "More" options
    • Formatting toolbar
  • Compose settings
    • Compose
    • When replying
    • When forwarding

The composer

The composer is where you can write your messages. Your message can be sent to recipients in different ways, and various actions can be taken on the message.

Compose in a new window

You can compose messages or replies in a new window by clicking the pop-out arrow icon in the upper-right hand corner of the composer:

You can also open the composer in a new window by holding the Shift key and clicking Compose or Reply.

For more information on using the pop-out composer, please see our Open messages in a new window help page.

Sending replies

Reply options

By default, the reply options you see on a message will depend on the recipients:

  • If you are the only recipient of a message, the reply button will be displayed as Reply, and the reply will go to the sender.
  • If you are a recipient on a message that was sent to a mailing list/listserve, the reply button will be displayed as Reply to list by default.
  • If you are a recipient on a message that has multiple recipients, the reply button will be displayed as Reply to all by default, and the reply will go to all other recipients listed on the message.

If you are viewing a conversation and you only want to respond to an individual sender, click the Actions button in the message and select Reply to sender. 

If you have already started drafting a message, you can click Reply to ___ in the composer and select the desired reply option.

If you prefer to have your replies go to the sender by default, this can be changed under Settings → Mail preferences (see "Replying in a conversation" on the Conversations help page for more).

Inline replies

When replying to a message in the web interface or desktop app, the compose window will appear inline within the conversation thread, allowing you to scroll up and reference the conversation if needed. Composer buttons (Send, Attach, Discard, etc.) will be shown along the bottom of the composer.

The subject line is hidden when replying inline to provide more space for writing your message. If you need to edit the subject line, you can do so by clicking the More button on the bottom toolbar, then clicking Edit subject. (Note: We generally do not advise changing a subject line on a reply, as this breaks conversation threading.)

Focused view

If you prefer to compose replies in a focused view (similar to the normal compose window), you can switch to the focused view by clicking the icon that looks like two arrows:

When replying in focused view, the composer buttons will be located at the top of the composer, and the subject line will always be shown.

If you switch to focused view, this preference will be saved locally.

Adding recipients

A message can be sent to one recipient or multiple recipients. 

Recipients can be added to the To field, Cc field, and/or the Bcc field. Clicking Cc and Bcc will display the Cc and Bcc fields, and you can click Hide to remove them. Recipients added to the Cc field will be carbon copied, and recipients added to the Bcc field will be blind carbon copied.

After adding a recipient, you can drag and drop them between To, Cc, and Bcc as needed. If you want to select more than one recipient at a time, you can use Ctrl + Click to select individual recipients, or Shift + Click to select a range of recipients. You can also right-click the recipient to show a menu where you can quickly add them as a contact, or view their contact information if they have already been added to your addressbook.

Composer toolbar actions

There are different actions that can be taken on a message. These are found on the composer toolbar, and include the Send, Save draft, and Discard actions.

Click Send to send your message to the intended recipients. There is also the Scheduled Send option, which can be accessed by clicking on the down arrow that is on the right side of Send. This is used for scheduling a later time in which your message will be sent out. For more details, see the Scheduled Send help page.

Click Save draft to save the message you're currently composing as a draft. For more details, see the Drafts help page.

Click Discard to delete the message you're currently composing.

"More" options

The More button in the composer toolbar shows extra options that you can enable for your message:

  • Show/Hide Cc: This option will toggle the Cc line on or off.
  • Show/Hide Bcc: This option will toggle the Bcc line on or off.
  • Edit subject: This option will only be shown if you are replying to a message in the web interface or desktop app (see Inline replies above).
  • Make plain text: This option will remove all formatting from your message and convert it to plain text. If you have plain text enabled, this option will show as Make rich text.
  • Mark high priority: This option will tell the recipient that you believe your message should be considered as urgent. 
  • Request read receipt: This option will request that the recipient notify you when they've read your message. 

More details on the high priority and read receipt options can be found in the Read receipts help page.

Formatting toolbar

There are various options available for formatting your messages in the composer. For a more detailed explanation of the formatting options, please see the Add formatting to emails help page.

If you prefer a distraction-free composing area, you can toggle the formatting toolbar on or off by clicking the A icon in the composer. The formatting toolbar can be toggled on/off in the web interface and desktop app only.

Compose settings

These settings can be found in Settings → Mail preferences.

Compose

This section includes settings you can apply when you are writing a message.

  • Default address: Set the address you want as the default when writing your messages.
  • Undo send: Enable or disable the period of time where you can undo the sending of a message.
  • Auto-save contacts: Enable or disable automatically saving addresses you communicate with to your contacts.
  • Compose format: Set the format of when you're writing a message to rich text or plain text. There is also an option to use the same format as the original message when you are replying.
  • Default style: Use the formatting section to set default styling for when you're writing your messages. The formatting added here will automatically apply when composing a new message or replying to a message.
  • Default email app: Choose to make Fastmail your default email app.

When replying

This section includes settings you can apply when replying to messages.

  • Reply from: Choose which address you want to reply from.
  • Default reply to: Choose the default behavior for when replying in an email thread.
  • Signature position: Choose where to place your signature when replying. For more information on signatures, please see the How to create a signature help page.
  • Include the original message: Choose how you want the original message to be shown in your reply.
  • Reply attribution: This is where you can modify your reply attribution line. For more details on this, see the Reply attribution help page.

When forwarding

This section includes settings you can apply when you're forwarding a message.

  • Signature position: Choose where to place your signature when forwarding. For more information on signatures, please see the How to create a signature help page.
  • Include the original message: Choose how you want the original message you're forwarding to be shown in your message.

articles.name: The Fastmail desktop app
articles.title: The Fastmail desktop app
articles.body:
This help page is for the Fastmail desktop app available on Windows, macOS, and Linux. If you're looking for information on the Fastmail mobile app available for iOS and Android, please see this page.

With the Fastmail desktop app, you can open Fastmail in its own window, separate from your web browser. Launch Fastmail directly from your dock or taskbar and find it in your platform’s app switcher.

You can download the desktop app here.

Navigation

Navigation in the desktop app generally matches navigation in the web interface.

Some differences may be visible in the top toolbar:

  • On the right-hand side of the toolbar, you'll find the Sync status icon (which looks like a cloud).  See Offline support in the desktop app below for more details.
  • If you are a Mac user and you have all apps toggled off in Settings → Display options, the left-hand side of the toolbar will display an Apps icon (which looks like 4 small squares). This can be used to switch between Fastmail's apps: Mail, Contacts, Calendar, Notes, Files, and Settings.

The desktop app also follows the same keyboard shortcuts as the web interface. A full list of available keyboard shortcuts is available here.

Offline support in the desktop app

Our desktop app offers full offline support. This means that even if you're not connected to the Internet, you can still read your mail, write replies, manage your calendar, and so on. 

If you've made any changes in the desktop app while offline, the changes will sync as soon as you reconnect to the Internet.

The Sync status icon indicates whether the app is currently fully synced, in the process of syncing, or offline.

For more information, please see our Offline support help page.

System requirements

The Fastmail desktop app can be run on the following OS versions:

  • macOS 12 (Monterey) or newer
  • Windows 10 or newer
  • Recent versions of Linux

Beta version

We also offer a beta version of the desktop app, which is available for download here.

For general information on using beta versions of Fastmail, please see our Fastmail beta help page.

articles.name: Offline support
articles.title: Offline support
articles.body:
With offline support, you can use the Fastmail mobile app or web interface even if you're not connected to the Internet. You can view and edit your mail, contacts, and calendars, and even reply to messages or make changes to your settings — any changes you make will be synced as soon as you're back online.

If you'd like to be able to access your mail while offline, you will first need to enable offline support for your device or browser (see Enable offline support below).

If you do not have offline support enabled, it is expected behavior to see a "Could not connect to server" banner over a loading screen when attempting to access Fastmail offline.

  • Enable offline support
  • Disable offline support
  • Limitations
  • Additional reading

Enable offline support

You can enable offline support for your device by going to Settings → Offline and clicking the toggle button next to Enable offline support.

We'll start downloading mail to your device so that it can be available for offline access. You can choose whether you'd like us to cache only recent mail (any message that has previously been viewed on this device, plus any future messages you receive) or if you'd like us to cache all mail (every message that's in your account).

The mobile app will need to stay open and active (not running in the background) while the device is syncing. Syncing on your browser can happen in the background.

Note: If you see a banner on the Settings → Offline screen that says "Long-term session required," this means that you will need to log out, then log back in with the Keep me logged in option enabled. Once you are logged in with Keep me logged in selected, you should then be able to return to the Settings → Offline screen and enable offline support.

Disable offline support

You can disable offline support for your device by going to Settings → Offline and clicking the toggle button next to Disable offline support, then selecting Confirm.

Disabling offline support will remove the cached data that we previously downloaded to your device while offline support was enabled.

Limitations

While offline, certain features may not be available or may behave differently.

Mail search

Mail search will only work on messages that have been cached offline.

Mail search cannot search inside attachments while offline.

Stemming is not used to match phrases while offline, which means that we won't automatically include plurals (fox, foxes) and tenses (fish, fishing, fished) in search results as we normally would. Offline mail search will instead use prefix matching, which means that when you search for a phrase, we will include any words that include that phrase at the beginning (e.g., searching fox would match "fox", "foxes", "foxtrot", etc.).

Snoozed mail

If you're offline when a snoozed message is scheduled to return to your Inbox, you will not see the snoozed message reappear until you're back online.

Calendar reminders

You will not receive calendar reminder notifications while offline.

Attachments

Attachments are only cached for offline use when opened on the device.

Attachments cannot be deleted from messages while offline. 

Account, billing, and security settings

You cannot make the following changes to your Fastmail account while offline:

  • Add, edit, or delete users
  • Add, edit, or delete custom domains
  • Make changes to your subscription plan
  • Update your billing details
  • Change any security-related settings 

Additional reading

If you're interested in the technical behind-the-scenes work that went into introducing offline support, check out our Fastmail Advent 2024 blog posts on the topic:

  • Dec 16: Offline support now in public beta
  • Dec 17: Building offline: general architecture
  • Dec 18: Building offline: syncing changes back to the server
  • Dec 19: Building offline: mail storage

articles.name: Troubleshooting Pobox migration problems
articles.title: Troubleshooting Pobox migration problems
articles.body:
On this page, we'll go over some common problems you might encounter while using Fastmail.

If you are looking for general information about migrating from Pobox to Fastmail, please see our Guide to Fastmail for Pobox users help page.

  • Unable to log in
  • Unable to receive any mail
  • Unable to send mail
  • I need help with something else

Unable to log in

If you are having trouble logging in, please check to make sure that you are logging in at app.fastmail.com and entering the correct username.

Your username should be the same as your Pobox reference address. Please be sure that you are entering the full email address, including the domain, into the login form. As an example, if your username is myaddress@domain.com, you will need to enter myaddress@domain.com instead of only typing myaddress.

If you have forgotten your username or password, or if you have lost your 2FA device, you can use our account recovery tool to regain access to your account.

We strongly recommend setting up a recovery email address and/or phone number in case you ever need to use the account recovery tool. You can set up recovery options by going to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen, finding the Account recovery section, and clicking Add recovery options. For more information on adding recovery options, please see our Passwords help page.

For more in-depth information on this problem, please see our I can't log in! help page.

Unable to receive any mail

There are several things that can cause problems with mail delivery, such as:

  • If your account is overdue
  • If your mail storage is full
  • If your custom domain is not working
  • If you have a rule that is sending mail to Trash
  • If you are using a mail client that has not been properly set up

For a complete guide that will walk you through troubleshooting this problem, please see our I'm unable to receive mail! help page.

Unable to send mail

If you see a warning in the Fastmail web interface that says "Send failed! Sorry, you can't send messages at this time," this means that we've detected bulk sending from your account. Fastmail is not designed for bulk sending, and our Terms of Service prohibits sending duplicative email. You will need to contact our support team to discuss next steps.

If you are having trouble sending from a mail client, please check that your SMTP settings are correct.

I need help with something else

If you are unable to find the cause of your problem, you may be able to find the information you’re looking for by searching Fastmail’s comprehensive Help Center.

If you would like assistance, please submit a ticket through our support form and our support team will be happy to look into this for you.

The support form is web-based, which means that you will be able to communicate with the support team even if your account is not able to send or receive mail.

articles.name: Subscriptions for migrated Pobox users
articles.title: Subscriptions for migrated Pobox users
articles.body:
All Pobox users were migrated to Fastmail in November 2024. If you are looking for information on submitting payment, or general information about migrating from Pobox to Fastmail, please see our Guide to Fastmail for Pobox users help page.

When you are migrated to Fastmail, you will be moved to a subscription plan that corresponds with your Pobox plan type.

Your subscription’s expiration/renewal date will stay the same, regardless of which Fastmail plan you are migrated to.

On this page, we’ll go over what you can expect from your new Fastmail plan.

We hope you love Fastmail as much as you've enjoyed Pobox for so many years, and continue to allow us to serve all your email needs for many more years to come.

Pobox Basic

Customers subscribed to the Pobox Basic plan were migrated to the Fastmail Lite plan. This plan comes with IMAP/POP/SMTP access, webmail access, 1 GB of mail storage quota per user, and up to 60 aliases. You'll also get calendars and contacts on the web and Fastmail mobile app, plus 100 MB of file storage.

We've added a bonus to the Fastmail Lite plan for Pobox customers: if you have a custom domain on your Pobox account, you will be able to continue using your domain at Fastmail at no extra cost. You can upgrade to a Fastmail Standard plan if you’d like to add more domains.

This plan will cost $24 per year.

Pobox Basic with AllMail and Pobox Plus

Customers subscribed to the Pobox Basic plan with AllMail or Pobox Plus will be migrated to the Fastmail Basic plan. This plan comes with IMAP/POP/SMTP access, webmail access, 5 GB of mail storage quota per user, and up to 600 aliases. You'll also get calendars and contacts on the web and Fastmail mobile app, plus 1 GB of file storage.

We've added a bonus to the Fastmail Basic plan for Pobox customers: if you have custom domains on your Pobox account, you will be able to continue using those domains at Fastmail at no extra cost. You can upgrade to a Fastmail Standard plan if you’d like to add more domains.

This plan will cost $36 per year.

Pobox Plus with AllMail and Pobox Mailstore

Customers subscribed to the Pobox Plus plan with AllMail or Pobox Mailstore will be migrated to the Fastmail Standard plan. This plan comes with IMAP/POP/SMTP access, webmail access, 50 GB of mail storage quota per user, up to 600 aliases, and support for custom domains. You'll also get calendars and contacts, which are accessible via the web, the Fastmail app, and CalDAV/CardDAV syncing, plus 10 GB of file storage with web and WebDAV access. Our Standard plan also includes Scheduled Send, Snooze, and calendar groups.

This plan will cost $60 per year.

Pobox Mailstore Jumbo

Customers subscribed to the Pobox Mailstore Jumbo plan will be migrated to the Fastmail Professional plan. This plan comes with IMAP/POP/SMTP access, webmail access, 100 GB of mail storage quota per user, up to 600 aliases, and support for custom domains. You'll also get calendars and contacts, which are accessible via the web, the Fastmail app, and CalDAV/CardDAV syncing, plus 50 GB of file storage with web and WebDAV access. Our Professional plan also includes Scheduled Send, Snooze, calendar groups, and an email retention archive for legal compliance.

This plan will cost $108 per year.

articles.name: Passkeys
articles.title: Passkeys
articles.body:
Passkeys are a passwordless method of signing into an account on a website or app. Instead of signing in to an account with a username and password, passkeys allow you to approve the sign-in using the same PIN, biometrics, or password that is set on your device.

Passkeys are considered more secure than passwords because they are cryptographic key pairs that are bound to a specific domain. This reduces the risk of phishing, as there is no password used and the passkey cannot be used on a fake website. Since there is no password to remember, this also allows for faster sign-ins and helps you avoid password reuse. 

Fastmail is introducing passkeys as an alternate login mechanism — your Fastmail username and password will continue to work after a passkey has been created in your account.

This help page will cover how you can use passkeys with your Fastmail account. If you'd like to learn more information about passkeys, the FIDO Alliance has published an FAQ here.

  • Creating a passkey
  • Logging in with a passkey
  • Managing your passkeys
  • Passkeys and 2FA

Creating a passkey

If you have never created a passkey in your Fastmail account, you can do so by following these steps:

  1. Go to Settings → Privacy & Security.
  2. Find the Passkeys section and click Create a passkey. 
    • A Verify it's you box may appear. Enter your password and click Continue. (For more information, see our Password-protected actions help page.)
  3. A new Create a passkey modal will appear. Click Continue.

  4. Your device or password manager will prompt you to create a passkey.

  5. Once you have successfully created the passkey on your device, you will see a Passkey created modal in the Fastmail interface. Give your passkey a name so that you can easily identify it later, then click Done.

After one passkey has been created in your Fastmail account, you can create any future passkeys by going to Settings → Privacy & Security and clicking Manage passkeys. From there, you can click Create a passkey and follow the above steps (starting from Step 3).

Logging in with a passkey

Once you have created a passkey, you can use it to sign in at the Fastmail login screen.

If you enter your username and we detect that your account has a passkey saved, we'll also show a button to begin the passkey sign-in flow. Once you have approved the sign-in using your device's password, biometrics, or PIN, you will be brought directly to your account's mailbox.

Depending on your password manager, you may be prompted to sign in with your passkey without needing to enter any credentials.

Managing your passkeys

You can view and manage your passkeys by going to Settings → Privacy & Security and clicking Manage passkeys.

From this screen, you will be able to see your passkeys listed from newest created to oldest created. You can see the passkey's name, when access was given, and when/where it was last used to access your Fastmail account.

If you want to delete a passkey, click the Remove button. Note that when a passkey is deleted from your Fastmail account, your device/password manager will not be aware of this change — you will continue to be prompted to use the passkey at the login screen until you have manually removed it from your device/password manager.

Passkeys and 2FA

Two-factor authentication is based on the idea that you are authenticating using a combination of something you know (your password), plus something you have (the 2FA code supplied by your device).

Passkeys already combine something you know/are (your PIN, password, or biometrics), plus something you have (your device). For this reason, we do not prompt for 2FA when passkeys are used.

articles.name: Guide to Fastmail for Pobox users
articles.title: Guide to Fastmail for Pobox users
articles.body:
We're pleased to share that, effective November 12, 2024, Pobox has merged with Fastmail! All Pobox customers have been migrated to Fastmail.

Fastmail is an email company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. Pobox has been owned and operated by Fastmail since its acquisition from IC Group in 2015. Since this acquisition, Pobox has been able to provide better webmail and customer service, all because of the expertise and staffing available through Fastmail. 

Your experience with Fastmail is brought to you by the same support agents and engineers you’ve enjoyed having on your side for many years, and we hope for many more years to come!

We’ve prioritized ensuring a smooth transition for all Pobox customers. Your mail will continue to be delivered, and your mail client setups do not need to change.

On this page, we will:

  • Go over the changes you can expect to see as part of the migration,
  • touch on the basics of using Fastmail, and
  • point you in the right direction for all of the features and actions you're familiar with in Pobox.

Every Pobox user received an email from us in October 2024. So that we can provide each user with the same high level of support, we sent this to a subset of customers each day.

If you have any questions or need assistance, you can contact Fastmail support anytime by sending an email to support@fastmail.com or submitting a ticket through our support form. Our support agents are knowledgeable about both Fastmail and Pobox, and will be happy to help you through this transition.

  • Logging in
    • Logged in sessions
  • Passwords and account security
    • Account recovery
    • 2FA
  • Mail
    • Webmail
    • Mail forwarding
    • Mail client setup
  • Calendars, contacts, and notes
  • Billing
  • Users & aliases
    • User management
    • Alias management
    • Delivery groups/forwarding by address
  • Personal domains
  • Spam
    • Trusted Senders
  • Filters
  • Access to Fastmail features
  • What if I already have a Fastmail account?

What’s new for all Pobox customers

Below you’ll find what you can look forward to now that your account is migrated to Fastmail.

Logging in

You will need to log in to your account through the Fastmail login screen at app.fastmail.com.  You will be able to log in using your Pobox reference address.

If you experience any difficulty logging in, please see the "Unable to log in" section of our Troubleshooting Pobox migration problems help page.

Logged in sessions

Fastmail offers unique features to help you keep track of when and where you are logged in, such as a login log and remote logout. For more information, see our Logged in sessions help page.

Passwords and account security

Your Settings → Privacy & Security screen is where you'll find everything you need to keep your account secure.

If you need to change your password, you can go to the Settings → Privacy & Security screen, find the Password & Two-step verification section, and click Change password. For more information on changing your password, please see our Passwords help page.

The Settings → Privacy & Security screen is also where you can go to create an app password to set up a third-party email client or app (e.g., Outlook, Apple Mail, Thunderbird). For more information on this, please see the Mail client setup section below.

Account recovery

We strongly recommend having a recovery email address and/or phone number in case you ever forget your password and need to use our account recovery tool. If you already have a recovery phone number in your Pobox account, this will be automatically added as a recovery option in your Fastmail account.

If you'd like to add or change your recovery contact details, you can do so on the Settings → Privacy & Security screen: find the Account recovery section, then click Add recovery options. We recommend taking this step as soon as you are able to access your Fastmail account.

2FA

We also recommend setting up two-step verification (also known as 2FA) to increase the security of your account. For more information on using 2FA, please see our Using two-step verification (2FA) help page.

If you already have 2FA options set up in your Pobox account, these have been migrated to your Fastmail account, so you will be able to continue using them with no additional setup needed.

Mail

You can now store mail in your Fastmail mailbox, read your mail on the web via Fastmail's exceptional web interface, and use IMAP to sync mail with the mail client of your choice. Sent messages are saved in your Sent folder.

Your mailbox storage quota corresponds with your subscription plan. See the Subscriptions for migrated Pobox users help page for details.

Webmail

Fastmail offers an intuitive webmail interface that comes with features to help you stay organized, productive, and secure.

You can choose to organize your mail in folders or switch to labels. You can also color code your folders or labels, and customize your entire user interface by choosing a theme.

Mail is threaded into conversations by default (i.e., replies are grouped with the original message).

For more information on navigating your mailbox, please see our Mail basics help section.

Mail forwarding

Your Pobox forwarding has been carried over to your Fastmail account. Messages sent to your Pobox aliases continue to be delivered to your forwarding addresses.

If you have been moved from a Pobox Basic or Pobox Plus plan, mail will be delivered to your forwarding addresses by default. Copies of your forwarded mail will be delivered to your Fastmail mailbox's Trash folder.

If you have been moved from a Pobox Mailstore plan, mail will be delivered to your forwarding addresses and your Fastmail mailbox.

Spam will not be delivered to external forwarding addresses. For more information, please see our Spam section below.

If you would like to set an alias to automatically forward all mail to an external email address (i.e., an address that is not set up in your Fastmail account), you can do this using the Deliver to another address option. For more information on setting this up, please see the Delivery options section of our How to set up aliases help page.

Mail client setup (IMAP, SMTP, and POP)

Anyone using a third-party email client or app (e.g., Outlook, Apple Mail, Thunderbird) prior to the migration should be able to use the same client—it should just work! No changes in server settings will be needed.

If you need to set up a new third-party email client or app, we recommend using Fastmail servers. We offer setup guides that can walk you through setting up your Fastmail account on various popular mail clients and apps.

When setting up a third-party email client or app, please note that all connections over third-party clients or apps need an app password to access your information. If you use your normal password or your Fastmail two-step verification password on an external client, syncing won't work and you will see a password error.

Our guides for several different mail clients and apps available in our Setting up mail clients help section. 

Calendars, contacts, and notes

We also offer built-in calendars, contacts, and notes, which can be easily synced with your devices.

Fastmail calendars allow you to keep track of upcoming events with ease. You can create events, send and respond to invitations, subscribe to public calendars, create shared calendars with other users in your account, and more.

With Fastmail contacts, you can add detailed entries to your address book, create VIP contacts that let you choose special settings for certain people, create a shared address book with other users in your account, or easily view contact information from your inbox using the sidebar.

Fastmail notes let you write, store, and easily access whatever information you need to stay organized.

Billing

Your Pobox invoice history is not available in the Fastmail billing interface. 

You can pay for your account and manage your subscription plan through the Settings → Billing & Plan screen. From this screen, you will also be able to view your account's billing history and next renewal date.

Please note that billing is only handled by the administrators of your account. If you are not an administrator for your account, you may not see this screen available in your settings. Separate billing contacts cannot be added.

Your subscription renewal date remains the same. When you renew, payments will appear on your credit card or bank statement as "Paddle.net* Fastmail."

For more information on billing, please see our Payments help page.

Users & aliases

User management

Each user has their own login credentials, mailbox, and storage quota.

If you want to add users to your account, you can do so by going to your Settings → Users & Sharing → User management screen.

If you are not an administrator for your account, you may not see this screen available in your settings.

For more information on adding and managing users, please see our Managing users as an admin help page.

Alias management

For most customers, your Pobox aliases have been migrated to your Fastmail account, so you will still be able to use all of your addresses.

There may be some edge cases where we will not be able to migrate a Pobox alias (e.g., the alias uses a custom domain that belongs to a user in a different Fastmail account). 

You can create new aliases by going to your Settings → My email addresses screen. For more information on navigating this screen, please see our My email addresses help page. 

When setting up a new alias, you'll see that you can set up delivery and compose options. Delivery options control how you receive mail sent to this alias (e.g., automatically moving a message to a certain folder or forwarding it to another email address) and compose options control how you send mail from this alias (e.g., changing the name recipients will see). For more information on configuring aliases, please see our How to set up aliases help page.

We also support plus addressing and subdomain addressing, which allows you to easily use variations of your aliases and automatically file mail into folders. For more information, please see our Plus addressing and subdomain addressing help page.

Delivery groups/forwarding by address

You can set up an alias to deliver mail to the addresses of your choice using the Deliver to another address option. For more information on setting this up, please see the Delivery options section of our How to set up aliases help page.

Personal domains

Personal domains set up in your Pobox account have been migrated to your Fastmail account. Your domains will continue working with no DNS changes or additional setup needed.

If you purchased a domain through Pobox, its registration will move to Fastmail. Please look for an email from us with instructions on how to ensure a smooth transition.

You can view domains that have been added to your Fastmail account by going to your Settings → Domains screen. On this screen, you will be able to see whether your domain is active or inactive, and if any DNS changes are needed. (Domains moved from your Pobox account will be shown as active, with no changes needed.) If you are not an administrator for your account, you may not see this screen available in your settings.

You can set up aliases using your custom domains by going to your Settings → My email addresses screen.

You can also set up a catch-all alias at your domain, which allows you to receive mail to any address at the domain, even if it has not been set up as an alias yet. For more information on setting up a catch-all alias, please see our Catch-all/wildcard aliases help page.

If you had AllMail set up for a personal domain in Pobox, a catch-all address has been automatically created in Fastmail. If you set up any AllMail exclusions, these were migrated over as well.

If you have been moved to a Fastmail Lite or Fastmail Basic plan, please note that you will not be able to add any new custom domains through Fastmail. If you wish to add a new custom domain, you will need to upgrade to a Fastmail Standard or Fastmail Professional plan.

If you have been moved to a Fastmail Standard or Fastmail Professional plan, you can add new custom domains by going to Settings → Domains, clicking Add domain, and following the domain setup wizard. You can purchase a custom domain through a registrar of your choice, or you can register a domain through Fastmail.

Spam

We hope you'll love Fastmail's improved spam protection, eliminating the need to manually fine-tune your spam handling. Fastmail's spam protection does not support blocking messages per country, emailed spam reports, or the "hold"/"release" process for filtering spam.

Messages that we flag as spam will be delivered to the Spam folder in your Fastmail mailbox, and will not be sent to your forwarding addresses.

If a legitimate message is caught in your Spam folder, you can use the Not spam button to mark it as such.

Upon marking a message as not spam, we'll check to see if your account has any mail rules or email address actions that should be applied to this message. We will apply any rules that would move the message to a folder or label, add a pin, mark the message as read, or send a copy to another email address. This means that if you have mail forwarding set up and you mark a message as not spam, the message should be forwarded accordingly. If the message does not match any rules, it will be moved to your Inbox. 

Your account's personal spam database is automatically trained with any spam messages you've deleted permanently from your Spam folder, and any non-spam messages you've moved out of your Spam folder. Once your personal database has seen more than 200 spam and 200 non-spam emails, it is automatically used to filter your incoming mail. You can expect your account's spam protection will improve over time as your personal database is trained. You can check how many spam and non-spam emails your account has learned by going to Settings → Filters & Rules and clicking Spam protection, then scrolling down to the Personal spam filter section.

Your Fastmail account's spam protection level is set to Standard, which sends messages with a spam score of 5 or higher to your Spam folder.

You can customize your account's spam filtering by going to your Settings → Filters & Rules → Spam protection screen. From here, you can choose your account's spam protection levels and customize other spam options. For more information, please see our Improving spam protection help page.

Trusted Senders

Fastmail supports whitelisting instead of the Trusted Senders section you are accustomed to. Your existing Trusted senders have been incorporated into Fastmail's spam protection to ensure that messages from addresses you've interacted with previously continue to be delivered.

Now that your account has been migrated to Fastmail, you can whitelist individual senders or domains by adding them to your contacts. 

You can add an individual address as a contact by going to your Contacts screen and clicking New contact. You can also add an individual address as a contact while viewing a message by clicking Show details, clicking the sender's email address, and selecting Add to contacts from the menu. This can also be done using the People tab of the sidebar.

If you would like to whitelist an entire domain, you can do so by adding the domain to your contacts using a catch-all address, which would look like adding *@domain.com as a contact.

If a legitimate message is caught in your Spam folder, but you do not want to whitelist the sender, use the Not spam button to automatically move the message out of your Spam folder and improve how your account filters spam for you in the future.

Filters

In the Fastmail interface, filters are referred to as rules. Rules can be used to automatically perform actions on incoming messages, such as moving certain messages into a folder. 

Your Pobox filters have not be automatically migrated to Fastmail as rules. You will need to manually recreate your Pobox filters as rules in the Fastmail interface.

You can create and manage your rules from your Settings → Filters & Rules screen. You can also create rules from a specific message or mailbox search.

From this screen, you can also manage your list of blocked senders. Mail sent from blocked senders and domains will be automatically moved to your Trash folder.

For more information on rules, including a list of available conditions and actions, please see our Flters & Rules help page.

For more advanced users, we also support rule creation using regular expressions and Sieve.

Access to Fastmail features

As part of the migration, you now have access to special Fastmail features designed to help you stay secure and productive. These features are available on all plans unless specified otherwise.

Masked Email
